papers.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: Abstract A two-step hyperparameter transfer framework predicts optimal learning rates for large Mixture-of-Experts models by scaling across widths and token budgets, enabling efficient pretraining without costly sweeps.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures significantly expand model capacity without a proportional increase in computational cost. However, optimizing their hyperparameters---particularly the learning rate---at extreme scales of both model size and token budget via sweeping remains computationally prohibitive. In this paper, we propose a compute-efficient, two-step hyperparameter transfer framework that estimates optimal learning rates for training large MoE models by transferring them across scaling model widths, and subsequently extrapolating to trillion-token horizons. First, we formulate a Maximal Update Parameterization (μP) adaptation for MoE architectures utilizing Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and the Muon optimizer, demonstrating that optimal learning rates transfer consistently across width-scaled models. Second, we extend this transferability along the token dimension by establishing a predictive scaling law. By applying linear regression to the optimal values derived from small proxy models on limited budgets, we successfully extrapolate the ideal learning rate to massive training horizons (e.g., 10 trillion tokens) with high fidelity (R^2=0.95). Consequently, this indicates that proxy training on small models is sufficient to determine the optimal learning rate for the extensive training of large-scale MoEs. We apply the proposed methodology to pretrain our foundation model (155B total, 17B active parameters) from scratch, and the stable training and evaluation results validate that optimal configurations for full-scale target models can be accurately predicted with minimal ablation costs.

ru.title: Трансфер гиперпараметров через масштабирование: от маленьких моделей к триллионам токенов
ru.desc: В статье предложена двухэтапная схема трансфера гиперпараметров для эффективного подбора скорости обучения (learning rate) в больших моделях Mixture-of-Experts без дорогостоящего поиска. Первый этап использует адаптацию Maximal Update Parameterization для архитектур MoE, которая позволяет переносить оптимальные значения learning rate между моделями разного размера. Второй этап устанавливает масштабируемый закон для экстраполяции learning rate на триллионы токенов через линейную регрессию на малых моделях. Подход позволяет предсказать оптимальные параметры для полномасштабного обучения 155-миллиардной модели, обучаясь только на маленьких прокси-моделях с высокой точностью (R²=0.95).

en.title: Efficient Learning Rate Prediction for Large MoE Models
en.desc: This paper introduces a two-step framework for predicting optimal learning rates in large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, which helps in efficient pretraining without extensive hyperparameter tuning. The authors utilize a Maximal Update Parameterization (μP) and Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) to ensure that learning rates can be effectively transferred across different model widths. They also establish a predictive scaling law that allows for the extrapolation of learning rates from smaller models to much larger training scenarios, achieving high accuracy. This approach demonstrates that training smaller proxy models can yield reliable learning rate configurations for training large-scale MoE architectures, significantly reducing computational costs.

zh.title: 高效预训练：超参数转移的新方法
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种两步超参数转移框架，用于预测大规模混合专家模型的最佳学习率，从而实现高效的预训练。该框架通过在模型宽度和令牌预算之间进行缩放，避免了昂贵的超参数搜索。我们采用最大更新参数化（μP）适应性和多头潜在注意力（MLA），证明了最佳学习率在宽度缩放模型之间的一致转移性。通过线性回归，我们成功地将小型代理模型的最佳学习率外推到大规模训练中，表明小模型的代理训练足以确定大规模混合专家模型的最佳学习率。

papers.title: Graph Engineering in the Era of LLM Agents: From Individual Intelligence to System Intelligence
papers.abstract: Abstract Graph Engineering organizes multi-agent LLM systems through dynamic graph structures to coordinate specialized agents and manage complex, evolving tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small LLMs have evolved from language generators to autonomous agents capable of complex, long-horizon tasks. This evolution has produced paradigms including Prompt Engineering to elicit model capabilities, Context Engineering to manage information access, Harness Engineering to organize external tools and resources, and Loop Engineering to support continual reflection and self-improvement. Yet as tasks grow more complex, individual intelligence faces a fundamental limit: many tasks require heterogeneous expertise, interdependent subtasks, parallel execution, independent verification, and persistent state, exceeding any single agent's organizational capacity. Augmenting one agent's capabilities or context cannot resolve this architectural mismatch; intelligence must instead be distributed across specialized agents and organized at the system level. We call this System Intelligence: an agent system's ability to organize and coordinate multiple intelligent components into a coherent, adaptive whole pursuing a shared objective. Achieving it requires more than adding agents; it demands explicit structures to organize work, coordinate heterogeneous agents, and maintain evolving execution states. We introduce Graph Engineering, an emerging paradigm for next-generation agent systems. Unlike prior paradigms that mainly optimize individual interactions or agent-level behavior, Graph Engineering constructs explicit, dynamic, evolving graph structures representing tasks, agents, and system states. These abstractions provide a unified foundation for organizing complex objectives, orchestrating heterogeneous agents, modeling system dynamics, and enabling scalable agent evolution. We systematically review the principles, methodologies, and applications of Graph Engineering for LLM agents. Related papers, open-source data, and projects are collected at https://github.com/DEEP-JLU/Awesome-Graph-Engineering.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Граф-инженерия: системный интеллект для многоагентных LLM
ru.desc: Статья представляет граф-инженерию как новую парадигму для организации многоагентных систем на основе LLM. Авторы утверждают, что по мере усложнения задач одиночные агенты достигают архитектурных ограничений и требуется распределение интеллекта между специализированными компонентами. Граф-инженерия использует динамические графические структуры для представления задач, агентов и состояний системы, обеспечивая координацию гетерогенных агентов и управление эволюцирующими вычислительными процессами. Подход объединяет предыдущие парадигмы (Prompt Engineering, Context Engineering, Harness Engineering, Loop Engineering) в единую систему, способную масштабироваться и адаптироваться к сложным многошаговым задачам.

en.title: Harnessing System Intelligence through Graph Engineering
en.desc: This paper introduces Graph Engineering, a new approach for organizing multi-agent systems using dynamic graph structures. It addresses the limitations of individual agents by distributing intelligence across specialized agents that can handle complex tasks collaboratively. The framework emphasizes the need for explicit structures to coordinate these agents and manage evolving tasks effectively. By doing so, Graph Engineering aims to enhance the overall system intelligence, allowing for better orchestration and scalability of agent interactions.

zh.title: 图形工程：智能体系统的新范式
zh.desc: 图形工程通过动态图结构组织多智能体大语言模型系统，以协调专业化的智能体并管理复杂的、不断发展的任务。随着大语言模型从语言生成器演变为能够执行复杂长远任务的自主智能体，出现了诸如提示工程、上下文工程、工具组织工程和循环工程等新范式。面对日益复杂的任务，单一智能体的能力受到限制，因此需要将智能分布在多个专业化的智能体之间，并在系统层面进行组织。图形工程作为一种新兴范式，构建了明确的动态图结构，以表示任务、智能体和系统状态，从而为组织复杂目标、协调异构智能体和支持可扩展的智能体演化提供了统一的基础。

papers.title: InfinityEdit: Infinite Video Editing with a Lightweight Edit-Ignition Adapter
papers.abstract: Abstract InfinityEdit enables continuous, unbounded video editing by using a lightweight adapter with history, temporal causal, and edit cross-attention modules to extend edits into future streaming frames while maintaining stability.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small With large pretrained models, existing methods have effectively improved instruction-based video editing. However, most of them rely on an in-place editing assumption. They align the edited video with the given source clip frame by frame over a fixed time span. This pattern fails for open-ended streams, e.g., restyling a live game or applying a camera move to an ongoing shot. In such cases, edits must extend to future frames as they arrive, rather than be applied to a static input clip. In this paper, we study this setting and name it infinite video editing: given a preceding segment and an edit request, a model must generate the next segment that continues the stream while applying the requested edit. This process repeats as an unbounded sequence of edit instructions arrives. This task brings two challenges: the edit must be a faithful continuation rather than a frame-wise rewrite, and generation quality must remain stable as edits accumulate. To address them, we first design a data-collection pipeline for infinite video editing. Based on the collected data, we propose InfinityEdit, a lightweight edit adapter that equips a streaming video generator with unbounded editing ability. The adapter contains three attention modules. History cross-attention guides the denoising frames using the input frames. Temporal causal self-attention keeps temporal cues flowing only from earlier frames to later ones. Edit cross-attention injects the edit request into generation. During inference, the adapter is activated only in the chunk where an edit request arrives. Subsequent chunks are generated by the original model with a reset anchor frame. This scheme applies the edit while preserving the original model's infinite generation ability. Extensive experiments show that InfinityEdit faithfully continues the stream under each edit, and stays stable over unbounded edit sequences.

ru.title: Бесконечное редактирование видеопотоков с сохранением стабильности
ru.desc: InfinityEdit решает задачу непрерывного редактирования видеопотоков в реальном времени, используя лёгкий адаптер с модулями внимания для истории, временной причинности и редактирования. В отличие от существующих методов, которые работают с фиксированными видеоклипами, система применяет правки к будущим кадрам по мере их поступления в потоке. Адаптер содержит три типа механизмов внимания: история помогает денуазации кадров, временная причинность сохраняет информацию от прошлого к будущему, а редактирование внедряет инструкции пользователя. Экспериментально доказано, что система стабильно применяет правки к неограниченной последовательности кадров без деградации качества.

en.title: Unbounded Video Editing with InfinityEdit
en.desc: InfinityEdit introduces a novel approach to video editing that allows for continuous and unbounded modifications in real-time video streams. Unlike traditional methods that edit static clips frame by frame, this technique enables edits to be applied to future frames as they are generated. The model utilizes a lightweight adapter with specialized attention modules to ensure that edits are seamlessly integrated while maintaining the quality and stability of the video. This advancement addresses the challenges of infinite video editing by ensuring that each edit is a coherent continuation of the previous content, rather than a simple frame-by-frame alteration.

zh.title: 无限视频编辑的未来
zh.desc: InfinityEdit 是一种新的视频编辑方法，能够实现连续和无限的视频编辑。它使用轻量级的适配器，结合历史、时间因果和编辑交叉注意力模块，能够在保持稳定性的同时，将编辑扩展到未来的流媒体帧。与传统方法不同，InfinityEdit 不再依赖于固定时间段的逐帧编辑，而是能够在视频流中实时应用编辑请求。通过这种方式，InfinityEdit 可以在不断到来的编辑指令下，生成高质量的连续视频片段。

papers.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs
papers.abstract: Abstract OmniAssistBench evaluates real-time interactive video assistants by reverse-engineering multi-turn interaction videos, revealing that current omni-modal models struggle with visual prompts, context retention, and timely responses.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) show great potential as real-time video assistants, which continuously perceive environments and guide users to achieve specific goals. Unlike traditional passive video understanding, interactive assistants should actively combine visual states, user goals, and prior knowledge to provide effective help. Evaluating this is rather challenging, as the model's unpredictable response dynamically changes the user's subsequent actions, which static offline datasets cannot accommodate. To address this bottleneck, we introduce OmniAssistBench. To solve the issue of diverging interaction paths where the same user goal can be achieved through various methods, we provide models with predefined priors derived from the source video, requiring them to guide users along the exact same routes. Since real interaction videos are rare, we construct the dataset by reverse-engineering existing Internet videos. We deduce logical user goals and segment the videos into multi-turn clips to simulate continuous interactions. This rigorous pipeline required over 1000 expert person-hours to build the dataset. Results show that the proprietary Gemini-3-Pro reaches 66.4 out of the max point of 100, while the open-source Qwen3-Omni-Instruct achieves 51.2. Although current models generally understand user inputs, they frequently provide incorrect or incomplete answers. Specifically, they struggle with visual prompts (e.g., hand gestures), fail to maintain historical context during multi-turn interactions, and fail to delay response until the target event. Results indicate substantial room for improvement before models can become reliable assistants.

ru.title: Интерактивные видео-ассистенты: почему модели не готовы помогать в реальном времени
ru.desc: OmniAssistBench — это бенчмарк для оценки омниmodальных больших языковых моделей в задаче интерактивного видео-ассистирования в реальном времени. Авторы решили проблему отсутствия подходящих датасетов путем обратного инженирирования существующих интернет-видео, извлекая из них цели пользователя и разбивая их на многооборотные взаимодействия. Результаты показывают, что современные модели, такие как Gemini-3-Pro и Qwen3-Omni-Instruct, испытывают значительные трудности с распознаванием визуальных подсказок, сохранением контекста между турами диалога и правильным определением момента для ответа. Исследование выявило критические пробелы в способности омниmodальных моделей работать как надежные интерактивные ассистенты.

en.title: Enhancing Real-Time Video Assistants with OmniAssistBench
en.desc: The paper introduces OmniAssistBench, a framework designed to evaluate real-time interactive video assistants, particularly focusing on omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs). It highlights the challenges these models face, such as handling visual prompts, retaining context over multiple interactions, and providing timely responses. To create a suitable evaluation dataset, the authors reverse-engineer existing videos to simulate multi-turn interactions, requiring significant expert effort. The results indicate that while some models show promise, they still struggle with accuracy and context management, suggesting a need for further development in this area.

zh.title: 提升互动视频助手的能力
zh.desc: 本论文介绍了OmniAssistBench，这是一个评估实时互动视频助手的工具。研究发现，当前的全模态大语言模型在处理视觉提示、保持上下文和及时响应方面存在困难。为了克服这些问题，研究者通过逆向工程现有视频构建了一个数据集，以模拟连续的用户交互。实验结果表明，尽管模型能够理解用户输入，但在提供准确和完整的回答方面仍有很大改进空间。

papers.title: ParaTempo: Efficient Parallel Reasoning via Temporal Confidence
papers.abstract: Abstract ParaTempo improves parallel reasoning efficiency by using temporal confidence to dynamically prune, retire, and reallocate reasoning branches without synchronization.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Parallel reasoning improves the accuracy and robustness of large reasoning models by exploring multiple solution paths, but its computational cost grows with reasoning depth and branch count. Existing methods for managing these parallel paths typically rely on final-answer consensus, local token confidence, or isolated intermediate probes. However, these signals are often delayed, weakly tied to actual reasoning progress, or too noisy for dynamic, branch-level control. To address these limitations, we introduce ParaTempo, a training-free asynchronous parallel reasoning framework. ParaTempo is driven by temporal confidence, a branch-local measure of answer-space convergence. Each branch is periodically probed for a tentative answer probability distribution, and temporal confidence quantifies how sharply the recent intermediate probes concentrate on a dominant answer. Once sufficient evidence has accumulated, ParaTempo drives its entire control process from this single signal: low-confidence branches are pruned, branches that persistently commit to their dominant answer are retired early, freed computation is reallocated by forking new branches, and generation stops globally once the confidence-weighted vote concentrates. Without requiring synchronization among reasoning trajectories, ParaTempo adaptively allocates computation based on branch-level convergence. Experiments on challenging mathematical and scientific reasoning benchmarks show that ParaTempo reduces average latency by 21.8-32.2% and total token usage by 18.1-30.3% while maintaining competitive accuracy. Moreover, temporal confidence exhibits stronger temporal stability and predictive power for future branch convergence than token-level and instantaneous signals.

ru.title: Адаптивное управление параллельными путями рассуждения через временную уверенность
ru.desc: ParaTempo — это система для параллельного рассуждения, которая использует временную уверенность для динамического управления ветвями вычислений без синхронизации. Вместо традиционных методов, полагающихся на финальный консенсус или локальную уверенность токенов, парадигма измеряет сосредоточенность промежуточных ответов на доминирующий результат. Система автоматически обрезает ненадёжные ветви, завершает ветви, которые стабильно приходят к одному ответу, и перераспределяет вычислительные ресурсы на новые перспективные ветви. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что ParaTempo снижает задержку на 21,8-32,2% и расход токенов на 18,1-30,3%, сохраняя точность решения сложных задач математического и научного рассуждения.

en.title: Boosting Parallel Reasoning with Temporal Confidence
en.desc: ParaTempo is a novel framework designed to enhance the efficiency of parallel reasoning in machine learning models. It utilizes a concept called temporal confidence, which helps in assessing how close a reasoning branch is to a correct answer. By dynamically managing branches—pruning low-confidence ones, retiring those that are confident, and reallocating resources to new branches—ParaTempo optimizes computational resources without needing synchronization. This approach not only speeds up the reasoning process but also maintains accuracy, as demonstrated by significant reductions in latency and token usage in various benchmarks.

zh.title: ParaTempo：高效的并行推理框架
zh.desc: ParaTempo是一种改进并行推理效率的框架，通过使用时间置信度动态修剪、退休和重新分配推理分支，而无需同步。它通过探索多个解决路径来提高大型推理模型的准确性和鲁棒性，但计算成本随着推理深度和分支数量的增加而增长。ParaTempo利用时间置信度作为分支局部的答案空间收敛度量，定期探测每个分支的答案概率分布，从而实现动态控制。实验表明，ParaTempo在保持竞争性准确度的同时，平均延迟减少了21.8-32.2%，总令牌使用量减少了18.1-30.3%。

papers.title: Beyond Correctness: Benchmarking and Aligning Response Behaviors in Hybrid-Thinking MLLMs
papers.abstract: Abstract Hybrid-thinking multimodal language models suffer from response-pattern misalignment between thinking and non-thinking modes, which is addressed by a diagnostic benchmark and pattern-specific reinforcement learning penalties.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Hybrid-thinking multimodal large language models (MLLMs) allow a single model to alternate between deliberative thinking and latency-efficient non-thinking inference. Although these modes differ in reasoning budget, their delivered responses should satisfy the same user-facing standard. Correctness alone may not characterize this response quality; we therefore evaluate task accuracy and response-pattern failures as complementary outcomes. We study this gap through response-pattern alignment: whether thinking and non-thinking interfaces preserve acceptable final-response behavior. We introduce PatternEval, a failure-enriched diagnostic benchmark comprising 2,415 multimodal prompts spanning visual perception and grounding, structured image understanding, and multimodal knowledge reasoning. PatternEval tests four recurrent failures: chain-of-thought leakage, response repetition, logical contradiction, and performative reasoning. Response-pattern failures are widespread across models from different providers, with non-thinking inference exhibiting substantially higher failure rates and thereby creating systematic misalignment between thinking and non-thinking interfaces. Motivated by this diagnosis, we develop PatternRM, a response-level reward model, and PatternRL, which introduces pattern-specific penalties during reinforcement learning. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-4B and Qwen3-VL-8B show that incorporating pattern-specific penalties into reinforcement learning can mitigate cross-mode misalignment while incurring a marginal task performance trade-off. Together, PatternEval and PatternRL provide an evaluation-and-training framework for aligning user-visible response patterns across hybrid-thinking interfaces.

Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Выравнивание паттернов ответов в гибридных многомодальных моделях
ru.desc: В статье изучается проблема несогласованности ответов между режимами с углубленным размышлением и быстрыми выводами в мультимодальных языковых моделях. Авторы представляют PatternEval — диагностический бенчмарк с 2415 мультимодальными примерами, который выявляет четыре типа ошибок паттернов: утечка цепочки рассуждений, повторение ответов, логические противоречия и формальное рассуждение. Они обнаруживают, что режим без размышления показывает значительно более высокий процент ошибок, создавая системное смещение между интерфейсами. Для решения этой проблемы предлагается PatternRL — метод обучения с подкреплением с патерн-специфичными штрафами, который уменьшает несогласованность между режимами при минимальном ущербе для качества задач.

en.title: Aligning Thoughtful and Quick Responses in Language Models
en.desc: This paper addresses the issue of response-pattern misalignment in hybrid-thinking multimodal language models (MLLMs), which can switch between thoughtful reasoning and quick responses. The authors introduce a diagnostic benchmark called PatternEval to evaluate the quality of responses, focusing on failures like logical contradictions and response repetition. They propose a reinforcement learning approach with pattern-specific penalties, named PatternRL, to improve alignment between the two modes of response. Experiments show that this method can reduce misalignment while maintaining acceptable task performance.

zh.title: 提升混合思维模型的响应一致性
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了混合思维多模态语言模型在思维和非思维模式之间的响应模式不一致问题。研究者们提出了一种诊断基准和模式特定的强化学习惩罚来解决这个问题。通过引入PatternEval基准，评估了模型在视觉感知、图像理解和多模态知识推理等任务中的响应模式失败。最后，论文展示了如何通过PatternRM和PatternRL来改善思维和非思维接口之间的对齐，尽管这可能会对任务性能产生轻微影响。

papers.title: Every Coin Has Two Sides: On the Dual Nature of Generalization in On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract On-policy distillation transfers reasoning behaviors rather than specific answers, with generalization strongly tied to teacher-student origin alignment and multi-teacher combinations causing capability trade-offs.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities by supervising trajectories sampled from the student's own policy, yet its generalization behavior remains poorly understood, as most studies evaluate OPD on a single domain and on benchmarks close to the training data. We present a controlled study that varies one generalization factor at a time, from in-domain distribution shifts to cross-domain transfer and the multi-teacher setting. We find that OPD transfers a teacher's reasoning behavior rather than its answers to particular problems: training difficulty barely matters, and even problems the teacher never solves are useful. Transfer depends strongly on the origin relationship between teacher and student: same-origin pairs bring the student close to the teacher across languages, reasoning horizons, and even other domains, whereas cross-origin pairs mostly fit the trained distribution. This broad reach is a double-edged sword: since routing prompts to domain experts cannot confine each teacher's influence, combining them yields a mixture-dependent seesaw among their capabilities. These results clarify when OPD generalizes and offer a useful perspective for diagnosing multi-teacher OPD.
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Дистилляция логики вместо ответов: как учитель учит ученика думать
ru.desc: В работе исследуется дистилляция в режиме онлайн (OPD), которая передаёт от учителя к ученику не конкретные ответы, а стратегии рассуждения путём обучения на траекториях, сэмплированных из политики самого ученика. Авторы проводят контролируемое исследование, варьируя факторы обобщения от распределений внутри домена до кросс-доменного переноса и работы с несколькими учителями. Результаты показывают, что OPD эффективнее передаёт логику мышления учителя, чем его ответы на конкретные задачи, и успех переноса сильно зависит от того, из одного ли источника происходят учитель и ученик. При комбинировании нескольких учителей возникает компромисс между их способностями, так как нельзя локализовать влияние каждого эксперта.

en.title: Learning to Reason: The Power of Teacher-Student Relationships in OPD
en.desc: This paper explores on-policy distillation (OPD), a method that helps a student model learn from a teacher model by following its reasoning processes rather than just copying answers. The study investigates how well OPD generalizes across different tasks and domains, revealing that the relationship between the teacher and student models significantly affects learning outcomes. It shows that using multiple teachers can create a balance of strengths and weaknesses, impacting the student's performance based on the teachers' backgrounds. Overall, the findings provide insights into optimizing OPD for better generalization in machine learning applications.

zh.title: 推理行为的转移：政策蒸馏的新视角
zh.desc: 本研究探讨了在政策蒸馏（On-policy distillation, OPD）中，教师的推理行为如何转移给学生，而不是具体的答案。我们发现，OPD的泛化能力与教师和学生之间的来源关系密切相关，且多教师组合会导致能力的权衡。通过控制实验，我们发现即使教师未解决的问题也能对学生有帮助，训练难度对结果影响不大。最终，这项研究为理解OPD的泛化能力提供了新的视角，尤其是在多教师设置下的应用。

papers.title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking
papers.abstract: Abstract EviRank reformulates multimodal image re-ranking as semantic constraint satisfaction by parsing queries into structured evidence packages and verifying candidates via rubric scoring and listwise comparison without training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Real-world image search queries are multimodal and compositional: ``find this shirt in pink'' specifies an entity to retain, an attribute to modify, and context to ignore. Yet existing re-rankers either compress such multifaceted relevance into an opaque embedding or rely on free-form chain-of-thought that easily omits or hallucinates fine-grained constraints. Drawing on rubric- and checklist-based evaluation from NLP, we recast multimodal image re-ranking as a semantic constraint satisfaction problem and propose EviRank, which parses any query - text-only, image-only, or composed - into a unified evidence package: typed criteria across six semantic slots (e.g., entities, attributes, relations), each labelled required, forbidden, or ignorable. Re-ranking then reduces to evidence-conditioned verification, combining deterministic rubric scoring and evidence-grounded listwise comparison in a single training-free procedure. The explicit evidence can further serve as structured supervision for optionally distilling a lightweight student. Across five benchmarks spanning text-to-image, image-to-image, and composed image retrieval, EviRank achieves state-of-the-art performance, and the distilled student preserves over 90% of the teacher's capability at substantially lower cost.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

ru.title: Переранжирование изображений через явное удовлетворение семантических ограничений
ru.desc: EviRank переформулирует задачу переранжирования многомодальных изображений как проблему удовлетворения семантических ограничений. Метод парсит запросы в структурированные пакеты доказательств, содержащие типизированные критерии по шести семантическим слотам (сущности, атрибуты, отношения), каждый из которых помечен как требуемый, запрещённый или игнорируемый. Переранжирование выполняется через комбинацию детерминированного рубрик-скоринга и списковой сравнительной оценки без необходимости обучения модели. Явная структура доказательств позволяет использовать её как супервизию для дистилляции облегчённой студент-модели, сохраняющей более 90% способностей учителя при значительно меньших вычислительных затратах.

en.title: EviRank: Smart Image Re-Ranking Through Structured Evidence
en.desc: EviRank is a novel approach to multimodal image re-ranking that treats the task as a semantic constraint satisfaction problem. It breaks down complex queries into structured evidence packages, which include specific criteria for entities, attributes, and relations. Instead of relying on opaque embeddings or free-form reasoning, EviRank uses deterministic rubric scoring and evidence-based comparisons to verify candidates. This method not only improves performance across various benchmarks but also allows for the creation of a lightweight model that retains most of the original's capabilities without the need for training.

zh.title: EviRank：多模态图像重新排序的新方法
zh.desc: EviRank将多模态图像重新排序重新定义为语义约束满足问题。它通过将查询解析为结构化的证据包，并通过评分和列表比较来验证候选项，而无需训练。该方法能够处理复杂的查询，明确区分所需、禁止和可忽略的条件。EviRank在多个基准测试中表现出色，且其轻量级学生模型在成本大幅降低的情况下，仍能保留超过90%的教师模型能力。

papers.title: UniSpace: Unified Visual Representation and Scalable Multimodal Modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract A reparameterized pretrained vision transformer unifies semantic understanding, high-fidelity reconstruction, and image generation within a single visual space without requiring a separate VAE.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Semantic vision encoders have become a central visual interface for multimodal understanding and semantic conditioning in image generation. However, their final tokens discard fine-grained visual details, leading to poor pixel reconstruction and limiting their use in reconstruction-sensitive tasks such as image generation and editing. In this work, we ask whether understanding, generation, and editing can be modeled in a single visual representation space built from a pretrained semantic ViT. We show that the frozen Transformer blocks of a semantic ViT are not intrinsically unable to preserve visual details. Instead, the original patch parameterization drives the representation toward semantic abstraction, making fine-grained information difficult to recover from the final tokens. Based on this observation, we introduce Patch Reparameterization, which preserves the original semantic pathway while adding a reconstruction-aware patch embedding that provides fine-grained visual information to the same frozen ViT blocks. The resulting unified representation preserves multimodal understanding while enabling high-fidelity image reconstruction and a favorable reconstruction--generation trade-off. We further scale this representation into UniSpace, an 8B Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts model that performs understanding, generation, and editing in the same visual space without a separate VAE pathway. System-level evaluations demonstrate practical text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing, showing that a reparameterized pretrained ViT can serve as a unified visual interface for scalable multimodal modeling.

ru.title: Единое визуальное пространство для понимания и генерации изображений
ru.desc: В работе предложен метод переопределения параметризации предобученного Vision Transformer, который объединяет семантическое понимание, высокоточную реконструкцию и генерацию изображений в единое пространство представлений без использования отдельного VAE. Авторы показали, что замороженные слои трансформера содержат достаточно информации для восстановления деталей, но исходная параметризация патчей смещает представления в сторону семантической абстракции. Предложенный метод Patch Reparameterization сохраняет исходный семантический путь и добавляет новое встраивание патчей с учетом реконструкции, позволяя получить точную визуальную информацию. На основе этого подхода построена модель UniSpace (8B параметров с Mixture-of-Experts), которая выполняет понимание, генерацию и редактирование изображений в одном пространстве представлений.

en.title: Unified Visual Space for Understanding and Generation
en.desc: This paper presents a novel approach called Patch Reparameterization that enhances the capabilities of pretrained vision transformers (ViTs) for tasks like image generation and editing. By modifying the way visual information is represented, the authors enable the model to retain fine-grained details while still benefiting from semantic understanding. The proposed method integrates high-fidelity reconstruction with multimodal understanding in a single visual space, eliminating the need for a separate Variational Autoencoder (VAE). The results demonstrate that this unified representation can effectively handle complex tasks such as text-to-image generation and instruction-based image editing.

zh.title: 统一视觉空间，实现理解与生成的完美结合
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出了一种重新参数化的预训练视觉变换器（ViT），它将语义理解、高保真重建和图像生成统一在一个视觉空间中，而无需单独的变分自编码器（VAE）。研究表明，传统的语义视觉编码器在生成图像时会丢失细粒度的视觉细节，导致重建效果不佳。为了解决这个问题，论文引入了补丁重新参数化技术，保留了原有的语义路径，同时增加了重建感知的补丁嵌入，从而提供细致的视觉信息。最终，提出的UniSpace模型能够在同一视觉空间中实现理解、生成和编辑，展示了其在文本到图像生成和基于指令的图像编辑中的实际应用。

papers.title: AgentMercury: Your Agent Can Synthesize Verifiable Environments for Business Scenarios at scale
papers.abstract: Abstract AgentMercury synthesizes scalable executable business environments that serve as generalizable reinforcement learning substrates, improving agent performance across enterprise and out-of-domain reasoning tasks while making environment construction itself learnable.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Agents learn to act through interaction with environments, yet the environments used for training are often manually constructed or synthesized around predefined tasks and benchmarks. This task-centric paradigm makes it difficult to scale environments that reflect realistic and evolving workflows where diverse tasks can naturally emerge from the underlying world. We introduce AgentMercury, a scalable framework for synthesizing executable environments from high-level business scenarios. Rather than constructing an environment for a specific task, AgentMercury first instantiates a persistent world with entities, services, tools, state, and executable cross-service invariants, from which diverse tasks and interaction trajectories can subsequently emerge. We construct 4,783 executable environments spanning 14 industries and 50 countries, and use them as training substrates for reinforcement learning. Despite being generated without targeting the evaluation benchmarks, policies trained on these business-oriented environments improve substantially on both enterprise workflows and out-of-domain benchmarks spanning reasoning, coding, scientific computing, and tool use. In our experiments, Qwen3.5-4B improves from 12.3 to 15.7 on EnterpriseOps-GYM and from 45.9 to 56.0 on AIME26 after training on AgentMercury environments. We further show that the construction process itself can be learned: fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on construction traces increases executable-world authoring success from 3.3% to 83.3% on held-out business scenarios. These results show that scenario-grounded environments can provide useful and generalizable learning signals beyond benchmark-specific training, while their construction can itself become a learnable capability.

ru.title: Обучаемые бизнес-сценарии как универсальный субстрат для агентов
ru.desc: AgentMercury — это фреймворк для автоматического синтеза масштабируемых бизнес-сценариев, которые служат универсальными окружениями для обучения агентов с подкреплением. Вместо создания окружений для конкретных задач, система генерирует персистентные миры с сущностями, сервисами и инвариантами, из которых естественным образом возникают разнообразные задачи. На 4783 синтезированных окружениях из 14 отраслей авторы обучили политики, которые улучшили производительность не только на корпоративных задачах, но и на вне-доменных бенчмарках по рассуждению, кодированию и использованию инструментов. Исследование демонстрирует, что сам процесс создания окружений можно обучить: модель Qwen3.5-35B достигла 83.3% успеха в авторингу новых сценариев вместо исходных 3.3%.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Scalable Business Environments
en.desc: AgentMercury is a framework that creates scalable and executable business environments for training reinforcement learning agents. Instead of building environments for specific tasks, it generates a persistent world with various entities and services, allowing diverse tasks to emerge naturally. This approach enables agents to learn from realistic scenarios across different industries and countries, improving their performance on both enterprise workflows and out-of-domain tasks. Additionally, the process of constructing these environments can be learned, significantly enhancing the efficiency of creating new training scenarios.

zh.title: AgentMercury：可扩展的智能体学习环境
zh.desc: AgentMercury 是一个可扩展的框架，用于从高层商业场景合成可执行的环境，旨在提升智能体在企业和跨领域推理任务中的表现。与传统的任务中心方法不同，AgentMercury 先创建一个持久的世界，其中包含实体、服务和工具，随后自然生成多样化的任务和交互轨迹。通过构建 4,783 个可执行环境，涵盖 14 个行业和 50 个国家，研究表明在这些商业导向环境中训练的策略在企业工作流和跨领域基准上都有显著提升。更重要的是，环境的构建过程本身也可以通过学习来优化，从而提高可执行世界的创建成功率。

papers.title: Partition the Support, Reconstruct the Residual: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation and World Models
papers.abstract: Abstract SparsePR accelerates video transformers via response-coupled partitioning and probe-fitted residual reconstruction, reducing attention error at low executed-pair densities with substantial speedups.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Training-free block-sparse attention can accelerate video transformers, but row-wise attention concentration does not by itself specify an executable sparse operator. Queries sharing a block route may have poorly overlapping supports, while retained attention mass alone does not determine the post-softmax error from skipped interactions. We show that partition geometry affects both pooled support and the predictability of the remaining residual from the sparse output. We introduce SparsePR, which combines Response-Coupled Partitioning with Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction. Sampled-query key responses form paired K/V groups, whose centroids induce query-response coordinates for shared routing. A small set of exact query rows then calibrates a call-specific affine correction from the sparse output within the output subspace observed in the probe residuals. Across four heterogeneous video generation and world models, SparsePR consistently reduces attention-reconstruction error. Ablations show that probe fitting accounts for most of this reduction, while response-coupled partitioning lowers hard-drop error and improves reconstruction under a finite probe budget. SparsePR preserves generation quality at 22.0-26.0% realized executed-pair density while achieving 1.48x-2.61x end-to-end speedups. Project page: https://pardistaghavi.github.io/SparsePR-website/

ru.title: Ускорение видео трансформеров через интеллектуальное разреживание внимания
ru.desc: SparsePR — это метод для ускорения видео трансформеров путём разреживания операций внимания (attention). Он использует Response-Coupled Partitioning для интеллектуального разделения запросов и ключей, а также Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction для восстановления потерянной информации из пропущенных взаимодействий. Метод калибрует коррекции на основе малого набора точных строк запросов, минимизируя ошибку реконструкции внимания. SparsePR достигает ускорения в 1.48-2.61 раза при сохранении качества генерации видео на уровне 22-26% плотности выполненных операций.

en.title: Accelerating Video Transformers with SparsePR
en.desc: The paper introduces SparsePR, a method designed to enhance the efficiency of video transformers by utilizing response-coupled partitioning and probe-fitted residual reconstruction. This approach minimizes attention errors while significantly speeding up processing times, achieving speedups of 1.48x to 2.61x. SparsePR effectively manages the distribution of attention across queries, ensuring that the most relevant interactions are preserved while reducing unnecessary computations. The results demonstrate that this method maintains high generation quality even with a low executed-pair density of 22.0-26.0%.

zh.title: SparsePR：加速视频变换器的创新方法
zh.desc: SparsePR是一种加速视频变换器的方法，通过响应耦合分区和探针拟合残差重建来减少注意力误差。该方法在低执行对密度下显著提高了速度，解决了传统块稀疏注意力的不足。我们发现分区几何形状影响了支持的聚合和稀疏输出的残差可预测性。实验结果表明，SparsePR在多个视频生成和世界模型中持续降低了注意力重建误差，同时保持了生成质量。

papers.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
papers.abstract: Abstract A small hybrid language model using sparse attention and short convolutions achieves faster CPU inference and better benchmark scores than larger conventional models despite training on far less data.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Small language models are usually built like large ones and then squeezed onto a CPU afterwards. We did the opposite: we fixed the target first, one user, one token at a time, 4-bit weights, ordinary CPU, and chose the architecture to suit it. The result keeps full attention in only 6 of its 18 blocks. The other 12 use short convolutions whose memory is two timesteps wide no matter how long the conversation gets, so two thirds of the network never re-reads a growing cache.   Trained from scratch on 59.9B tokens, the model scores 47.31 on a five-task benchmark against a bar of 42.20 that was fixed before training began. It beats GPT-2 124M, Pythia-160M, OPT-125M and GPT-neo-125M, all trained on three to six times more data, and exceeds MobileLLM-125M's published score despite that model seeing a trillion tokens. Validation bits-per-byte is 0.8685.   To check the architecture rather than the training recipe, we trained a conventional all-attention model of the same size on the same data, and wrote down the winning condition before scoring either. The hybrid won the chosen quality metric by 0.81%, matched it on downstream tasks, produced a 6.3% smaller 4-bit file, and decoded 1.76x faster at 2048 tokens of context, 2.08x against an external model of similar size. In every measurement the speed advantage is near zero at an empty context and grows with length, which is what the mechanism predicts and what a merely leaner model would not show. A simple bandwidth calculation predicts only 1.17x, so memory volume alone does not explain the gap.   We also report what did not work: an unmitigated 4-bit quality cost, roughly half the convolution channels ending up inert and impossible to remove, and a vocabulary larger than this model size warrants.

ru.title: Гибридная архитектура: разреженное внимание и свёртки для эффективного вывода на CPU
ru.desc: В статье описывается гибридная языковая модель, которая достигает быстрого вывода на CPU благодаря комбинации полного внимания только в 6 из 18 блоков и коротких свёрток в остальных блоках. Архитектура была спроектирована с учётом целевого оборудования с самого начала - модель использует 4-битные веса и работает с памятью размером всего два временных шага, что позволяет избежать переиспользования растущего кэша. Несмотря на обучение на значительно меньшем количестве данных (59.9B токенов), модель превзошла GPT-2, Pythia и другие базовые модели того же размера, обученные на 3-6 раз большем объёме данных. Исследование включало контролируемое сравнение с обычной моделью на основе полного внимания и продемонстрировало 1.76-2.08x ускорение декодирования с растущим преимуществом при увеличении контекста.

en.title: Efficient Language Modeling with Sparse Attention and Convolutions
en.desc: This paper presents a small hybrid language model that utilizes sparse attention and short convolutions to achieve efficient CPU inference. Unlike traditional models that are scaled down after training, this model was designed specifically for a single user and token at a time, resulting in faster performance and better benchmark scores. It was trained on 59.9 billion tokens and outperformed larger models like GPT-2 and Pythia, despite using significantly less data. The architecture allows for full attention in only a portion of the model, optimizing memory usage and processing speed as conversation length increases.

zh.title: 小型混合模型，速度与性能双优！
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种小型混合语言模型，它使用稀疏注意力和短卷积，尽管训练数据远少于传统大型模型，但在CPU推理速度和基准测试分数上表现更好。该模型的架构是针对特定目标设计的，采用4位权重和普通CPU，保持了18个模块中6个的全注意力，其余12个使用短卷积，确保内存使用效率。模型在训练时使用了59.9亿个标记，在五项任务基准测试中得分47.31，超越了多种大型模型。通过与传统全注意力模型的比较，混合模型在质量指标上胜出，并在速度上表现出显著优势。

papers.title: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
papers.abstract: Abstract RecVerse is a GUI-grounded agent that uses hierarchical memory and trajectory-level reinforcement learning to simulate realistic multi-turn e-commerce shopping sessions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Simulating realistic user shopping behavior underpins offline evaluation and reinforcement learning in e-commerce scenarios. While recent LLM- and VLM-based simulators have made encouraging progress, reproducing a real browsing session remains difficult for two reasons. (i) Memory Challenge: a shopping session spans dozens of pages, yet existing agents either discard long-range observation histories, losing the evolving user state, or naively concatenate them, overwhelming the context window and even degrading simulation quality. (ii) Optimization Challenge: current user simulators are typically supervised to match each logged action via imitation or step-level rewards; the resulting sessions often display unrealistic patterns, such as over-exploration or excessive passivity, which per-step supervision can neither detect nor correct.   To address the above challenges, we present RecVerse, a GUI-grounded simulation agent that perceives pages through screenshots and produces faithful multi-turn trajectories. For the memory challenge, RecVerse adopts a cognitive-inspired hierarchical memory: Working Memory for short-term focus, Episodic Memory for in-session traces, and Preference Memory for high-level intent, with memory updates treated as actions so that the agent adaptively learns when and what to memorize. For the optimization challenge, RecVerse is optimized with a trajectory-level RL objective that scores entire sessions, aligning both macro-level action-type distributions and micro-level shopping intent with real users. We further release USB (User Simulation Benchmark), an interactive e-commerce GUI trajectory dataset for multi-turn user simulation. Experiments show that RecVerse significantly outperforms existing baselines in both behavioral fidelity and intent consistency.

ru.title: Иерархическая память и траекторное обучение для реалистичной симуляции пользователей в e-commerce
ru.desc: RecVerse — это GUI-агент, который симулирует реалистичные многоходовые сессии покупок в электронной коммерции, используя иерархическую память и обучение с подкреплением на уровне траекторий. Агент решает две ключевые проблемы: вызов памяти (система хранит долгосрочную историю через рабочую память для краткосрочного фокуса, эпизодическую память для сессионных следов и память предпочтений для высокоуровневых намерений) и проблему оптимизации (траекторный RL-объектив оценивает целые сессии, согласуя распределения действий и намерения с реальными пользователями). Авторы представляют USB — интерактивный датасет GUI-траекторий для симуляции пользователей в многоходовых сценариях. Экспериментальные результаты демонстрируют превосходство RecVerse над существующими базовыми моделями в точности поведения и согласованности намерений.

en.title: RecVerse: Realistic E-Commerce Simulation through Hierarchical Memory and Reinforcement Learning
en.desc: RecVerse is an advanced agent designed to simulate realistic e-commerce shopping experiences using hierarchical memory and trajectory-level reinforcement learning. It addresses the memory challenge by implementing a cognitive-inspired memory system that categorizes information into Working, Episodic, and Preference memories, allowing the agent to effectively manage long-term user states. To tackle the optimization challenge, RecVerse employs a trajectory-level reinforcement learning approach that evaluates entire shopping sessions, ensuring that the agent's actions reflect genuine user behavior. The introduction of the User Simulation Benchmark (USB) dataset further enhances the evaluation of multi-turn user simulations, demonstrating RecVerse's superior performance in mimicking real user intent and behavior.

zh.title: 真实购物体验的智能模拟
zh.desc: RecVerse 是一个基于图形用户界面的智能体，利用层次记忆和轨迹级强化学习来模拟真实的多轮电子商务购物会话。它通过屏幕截图感知页面，并生成真实的多轮轨迹，以应对购物会话中的记忆和优化挑战。RecVerse 采用了认知启发的层次记忆结构，能够有效地处理长时间的用户状态变化。实验结果表明，RecVerse 在行为真实度和意图一致性方面显著优于现有的基线模型。

papers.title: Llama-Mobile: Efficient 2.7-Bit Quantization of VLMs
papers.abstract: Abstract A framework quantizes vision-language models for mobile deployment using self-generated training data and a 2.7-bit format, compressing Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct to 3.7 GB with preserved visual question answering performance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Deploying vision-language models (VLMs) on mobile devices is challenging due to their significant memory and compute requirements. We present a framework for quantizing VLMs for efficient inference on resource-constrained hardware. Our approach combines a quantization pipeline that uses the model itself to generate training data and does not require access to the training setup, with a novel 2.7-bit-per-parameter format supporting efficient execution on Arm CPUs. We validate our approach by compressing the Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct model to 3.7 GB with 8-bit activations, preserving strong performance on a set of standard visual question answering tasks.

ru.title: Компактные зрительно-языковые модели для мобильных устройств через самогенерируемую квантизацию
ru.desc: В работе предложена методология квантизации зрительно-языковых моделей для развертывания на мобильных устройствах. Авторы используют инновационный подход, при котором сама модель генерирует данные для обучения квантизационного процесса без доступа к исходным тренировочным наборам. Разработан специальный формат с глубиной в 2,7 бита на параметр, который позволяет эффективно выполнять вычисления на процессорах архитектуры Arm. Демонстрируется успешное сжатие модели Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct до 3,7 ГБ при сохранении высокого качества на задачах визуального вопросно-ответного взаимодействия.

en.title: Efficient Mobile Vision-Language Models with 2.7-Bit Quantization
en.desc: This paper introduces a framework for quantizing vision-language models (VLMs) to make them suitable for mobile devices. It utilizes a self-generated training data approach, allowing the model to create its own training examples without needing the original training setup. The framework employs a unique 2.7-bit format for parameters, which significantly reduces the model size while maintaining performance. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their method by compressing the Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct model to 3.7 GB, ensuring it still performs well on visual question answering tasks.

zh.title: 高效量化视觉语言模型，助力移动部署
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种框架，用于将视觉语言模型（VLMs）量化，以便在移动设备上高效部署。该框架利用模型自身生成训练数据，并采用一种新的2.7位参数格式，从而在资源受限的硬件上实现高效推理。通过这种方法，我们成功将Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct模型压缩到3.7 GB，同时在标准视觉问答任务上保持了良好的性能。此研究为在移动设备上应用复杂的视觉语言模型提供了新的解决方案。

papers.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
papers.abstract: Abstract Hydra-0 uses action flow as a shared visual interface for generalist world modeling and robot control across diverse embodiments and tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce Hydra-0, a generalist world model conditioned on action flow, which represents robot actions as pixel motion. This shared visual interface enables generalist world modeling and control by learning action consequences across embodiments, tasks, environments, and video-generation backbones. Our best configuration achieves 90.4% lower robot-motion error and 60.2% lower object-motion error than our action-conditioned baseline, while supporting zero-shot composition and data-efficient adaptation. On the RoboLab benchmark, Hydra-0 achieves a Pearson correlation of r=0.96 between replayed and reference success rates. Finally, we uncover an emergent inverse mode of this interface: a world action model that predicts compatible robot motion from desired object flow transferred from a human demonstration. A trained action head maps the resulting latent features to executable actions without requiring task-specific expert robot demonstrations. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of action flow as a shared control interface connecting heterogeneous training data, open-loop policy evaluation, and robot control.

ru.title: Единый визуальный язык действий для управления роботами разных типов
ru.desc: Hydra-0 — это обобщённая модель мира, которая использует поток действий (представление действий робота как движения пикселей) в качестве единого визуального интерфейса для управления роботами различной конструкции. Модель обучается предсказывать последствия действий через разные воплощения робота, задачи и окружения, достигая значительного снижения ошибок в движении робота и объектов. Система демонстрирует нулевой shot композицию, эффективную адаптацию с малым количеством данных и высокую корреляцию между предсказанными и реальными результатами на бенчмарке RoboLab. Кроме того, модель обнаруживает обратный режим работы — предсказание движения робота на основе желаемого потока движения объекта из человеческих демонстраций без необходимости в специфических для каждой задачи данных обучения.

en.title: Hydra-0: Revolutionizing Robot Control with Action Flow
en.desc: Hydra-0 is a novel generalist world model that utilizes action flow to create a visual interface for robot control and world modeling. By representing robot actions as pixel motion, it allows for learning the consequences of actions across various tasks and environments. The model significantly reduces robot-motion and object-motion errors compared to previous methods, while also enabling zero-shot learning and efficient adaptation to new tasks. Additionally, it introduces a unique capability to predict robot motions based on human demonstrations, enhancing its versatility in robot control applications.

zh.title: 动作流：连接机器人控制与世界建模的桥梁
zh.desc: Hydra-0 是一种通用世界模型，利用动作流作为共享的视觉接口，能够在不同的机器人和任务中进行建模和控制。它通过将机器人动作表示为像素运动，学习不同环境和任务中的动作后果，从而实现更高效的控制。与传统的基线相比，Hydra-0 在机器人运动误差和物体运动误差上分别降低了 90.4% 和 60.2%。此外，它还支持零-shot 组合和数据高效适应，展示了动作流作为连接异构训练数据和机器人控制的潜力。

papers.title: Human-Centric Intelligence in the Era of Foundation Models: A Survey
papers.abstract: Abstract This survey proposes a unified taxonomy and methodological framework for human-centric intelligence across visual, dynamic, and embodied levels within the foundation-model era.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Human-centric intelligence is evolving in the foundation-model era, with growing emphasis on scale, transferability, and general-purpose modeling. Yet it has not fully integrated with foundation models to achieve the comparable progress seen in them. More importantly, recent advances across this broad landscape remain fragmented across tasks, modalities, and research communities, leaving their intrinsic conceptual and methodological connections unclear. To bridge these divides and rethink human-centric intelligence in the foundation-model era, we introduce a full-spectrum human context taxonomy that integrates six interconnected levels by viewing humans as observable subjects through visual appearance and spatial geometry, as dynamic actors through kinematic dynamics and interaction modeling, and as situated agents through world simulation and embodied agency. We next present the methodological foundations of the field, covering human-centric data families, computational architecture paradigms, and representative training and inference optimization strategies. We then systematically review representative methods across these levels and organize the associated datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation metrics. We further discuss open challenges and promising research directions toward human-centric intelligence that is scalable, trustworthy, physically grounded, and deployable, aiming to provide a coherent framework and practical reference for advancing the field. Finally, we provide a systematically organized and continuously updated collection of human-centric AI literature and resources on our project page.
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project

ru.title: Единая таксономия для понимания человека в эпоху foundation models
ru.desc: Статья представляет единую таксономию и методологический framework для понимания человеческого поведения в эпоху foundation models, охватывающий три уровня: визуальный анализ внешности и геометрии, динамическое моделирование движений и взаимодействий, а также симуляцию поведения агентов в окружающем мире. Авторы систематизируют фрагментированные исследования в области компьютерного зрения и анализа человека, предлагая единый методологический подход, основанный на масштабируемых foundation models. В работе подробно рассматриваются архитектуры моделей, стратегии обучения и оптимизации, а также представляются наборы данных и метрики для оценки. Цель исследования — создать практический reference для разработки надёжных, физически обоснованных и применимых систем для понимания и анализа человеческого поведения.

en.title: Bridging Human-Centric Intelligence in the Foundation-Model Era
en.desc: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for understanding human-centric intelligence in the context of foundation models. It emphasizes the need for integration across various tasks and modalities to enhance the scalability and transferability of human-centric AI. The authors propose a taxonomy that categorizes human interactions into visual, dynamic, and embodied levels, facilitating a clearer understanding of these concepts. Additionally, the paper reviews existing methodologies and datasets, highlighting challenges and future directions for research in this evolving field.

zh.title: 整合人本智能，推动基础模型时代的进步
zh.desc: 本调查提出了一个统一的分类法和方法框架，旨在在人本智能的基础模型时代整合视觉、动态和具身层面。人本智能正在发展，但尚未与基础模型充分整合，导致在任务、模态和研究社区之间的进展碎片化。我们引入了一个全谱人类背景分类法，整合了六个相互关联的层次，强调人类作为可观察的主体、动态行为者和具身代理的多重角色。最后，我们讨论了人本智能的开放挑战和未来研究方向，旨在为该领域的进步提供一个连贯的框架和实用参考。

papers.title: PhysCaP: Grounding Code-as-Policy Agent with Physics-Informed Exploration
papers.abstract: Abstract PhysCaP is a physics-informed code-generation agent that actively explores objects to infer hidden physical properties for efficient robotic manipulation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present PhysCaP, a Physics-Informed Code-as-Policy agent for active perception in robotic manipulation. While vision-language-action policies excel at imitating demonstrations, they rely on passive observation and fail to infer latent physical properties critical for manipulation. PhysCaP augments code-as-policy frameworks with a physics-informed exploration layer that enables explicit information-seeking through interaction. It introduces training-free physical property extraction modules that estimate object mass and stiffness from robot proprioception without additional sensors. To balance exploration costs and the efficiency of information obtained, PhysCaP employs a dual-agent design: a Planner that decides when to explore and when to stop, and a Prioritizer that filters implausible interactions and ranks the remainder using a heuristic priority score, enabling efficient, targeted exploration. We evaluate PhysCaP on real-world tabletop manipulation tasks (searching for hidden objects, detecting empty cans, and finding ripe avocados) and a simulated task in LIBERO. The results show that existing passive and naive interactive baselines either fail when physical properties are hidden or over-explore, whereas PhysCaP achieves comparable performance with fewer interactions and reduced execution time. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed physical property extraction modules. Project page: https://physcap.github.io
affiliations: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

ru.title: Активное исследование скрытых свойств объектов для умного робота
ru.desc: PhysCaP — это агент для генерации кода, который использует знания физики для активного исследования объектов при выполнении задач робототехнического манипулирования. Система расширяет подход code-as-policy дополнительным слоем активного восприятия, позволяя роботу целенаправленно взаимодействовать с объектами для выявления скрытых физических свойств. PhysCaP использует двухагентную архитектуру: Планировщик решает, когда исследовать объект, а Приоритизатор отбирает эффективные взаимодействия, оценивая их полезность. На реальных задачах манипулирования система достигает лучшей производительности, чем пассивные методы, при этом требуя значительно меньше взаимодействий с объектом.

en.title: Unlocking Hidden Properties for Smarter Robot Manipulation
en.desc: PhysCaP is a novel agent designed for robotic manipulation that uses physics-informed code generation to uncover hidden physical properties of objects. Unlike traditional methods that rely on passive observation, PhysCaP actively interacts with objects to gather critical information such as mass and stiffness without needing extra sensors. It features a dual-agent system, consisting of a Planner that manages exploration decisions and a Prioritizer that evaluates and ranks potential interactions based on their usefulness. The results demonstrate that PhysCaP outperforms existing methods by achieving similar outcomes with fewer interactions and less time spent on tasks.

zh.title: 物理驱动的智能探索，提升机器人操作效率
zh.desc: PhysCaP是一种物理信息驱动的代码生成代理，旨在通过主动探索物体来推断隐藏的物理属性，以提高机器人操作的效率。与传统的视觉-语言-动作策略不同，PhysCaP能够通过交互主动获取信息，而不仅仅依赖被动观察。它引入了无需额外传感器的物理属性提取模块，能够从机器人自身的感知中估计物体的质量和刚度。通过双代理设计，PhysCaP有效平衡了探索成本和信息获取效率，展示了在实际操作任务中的优越性能。

papers.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Abstract CLEAR uses a hidden-state gate to continuously modulate a safety low-rank adapter, improving LLM safety while preserving utility on benign inputs.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Improving the safety of large language models (LLMs) often comes at the expense of utility, as globally applied safety tuning may affect model responses to both harmful and benign inputs. We propose Continuous LatEnt Adapter Routing (CLEAR), a conditional safety adaptation framework that uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously control the activation strength of a safety low-rank adapter. CLEAR aims to reduce harmful completions while avoiding unnecessary changes to the frozen backbone that could degrade performance on benign prompts. Experiments on widely used safety and utility benchmarks show that CLEAR improves robustness on HarmBench while reducing the utility degradation observed with globally applied safety tuning such as SFT or standard low-rank adaptation (LoRA). On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, CLEAR reduces HarmBench ASR from 32.3\% to 0.5\%, while retaining most of the base model's utility and achieving up to 7.1 percentage points higher GSM8K accuracy than globally applied SFT or LoRA. These results suggest that CLEAR is a promising mechanism for improving the safety--utility trade-off in LLM alignment.
affiliations: Siebel School of Computing and Data Science, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

ru.title: Селективная защита без потери функциональности
ru.desc: В статье предложена система CLEAR, которая использует скрытое состояние нейронной сети для управления адаптером безопасности с низким рангом. Этот подход позволяет избирательно применять защиту от опасных запросов, не влияя на качество ответов на безвредные входные данные. Авторы показывают, что CLEAR значительно снижает количество вредоносных ответов модели Llama-3-8B-Instruct, одновременно сохраняя её производительность на стандартных тестах. Таким образом, предложенный метод решает критическую проблему компромисса между безопасностью и полезностью больших языковых моделей.

en.title: Enhancing LLM Safety Without Sacrificing Utility
en.desc: The paper introduces CLEAR, a framework designed to enhance the safety of large language models (LLMs) without sacrificing their utility. It employs a hidden-state gate to dynamically adjust the influence of a safety low-rank adapter, allowing for better control over model responses. This approach minimizes harmful outputs while maintaining performance on benign inputs, addressing the common trade-off between safety and utility. Experimental results demonstrate that CLEAR significantly reduces harmful completions and improves accuracy on various benchmarks compared to traditional safety tuning methods.

zh.title: CLEAR：提升大语言模型的安全性与效用平衡
zh.desc: CLEAR是一种条件安全适应框架，利用隐藏状态门控技术来持续调节安全低秩适配器的激活强度。该方法旨在减少有害输出，同时避免对基础模型的过度修改，以保持在良性输入上的性能。实验结果表明，CLEAR在HarmBench基准测试中显著提高了模型的鲁棒性，并减少了全球安全调优带来的效用下降。CLEAR在Llama-3-8B-Instruct模型上将HarmBench的有害完成率从32.3%降低到0.5%，同时在GSM8K准确率上比传统方法提高了7.1个百分点。

papers.title: Peer-Voted LLM-Agent Stress Tests Find Feed-Induced Lexical Convergence but No Reliable Matched-Exposure Advantage for Distributed Sources
papers.abstract: Abstract Peer-ranked feeds of synthetic LLM agents increase lexical convergence but do not reliably produce opinion capture or coordination advantages across model families and topics.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Population-level behavior in large-language-model (LLM) agents cannot be characterized by single-agent benchmarks. We introduce PV-SST, a peer-voted social-platform testbed, and report a separately frozen, preregistered matched-exposure experiment spanning four topics, four unused seeds, four open-weight model families, and three prespecified larger variants. The experiment comprises 448 trials and 112 complete model-by-topic-by-seed blocks. Relative to a topic-only control, a feed of previous-round peer posts ranked by peer-generated likes increases final-round lexical similarity in both the four-family core panel (paired mean difference +0.0082 TF-IDF cosine units, 95% block-bootstrap CI [0.0043, 0.0121], randomization p=0.000105, n=64 blocks) and the three-variant size extension (+0.0109 [0.0069, 0.0151], p=0.000001, n=48). This contrast bundles peer-post exposure with ranking and therefore does not identify a ranking-only effect. Opposite-side survival falls in the core panel (-3.9 percentage points [-6.8, -1.6], p=0.0068) but not conclusively in the larger variants (-1.0 pp [-3.1, 0.4], p=0.50). Holding adversarial impressions fixed, four distributed sources do not reliably move honest-agent stance more than one source. The preregistered distributed-minus-single contrast is positive but inconclusive in the core panel (+0.057 [-0.009, 0.125], p=0.112) and negative in the larger variants (-0.040 [-0.113, 0.035], p=0.332), failing the prespecified cross-model and cross-topic consistency criterion. Thus the robust result is lexical convergence under the tested peer-ranked feed, not general opinion capture or a general coordination advantage. The study evaluates synthetic LLM-agent populations; it does not estimate effects on people or production platforms.

ru.title: Слова сходятся, мнения — нет: о пределах влияния социальных сетей на LLM-агентов
ru.desc: Исследователи создали платформу PV-SST для изучения поведения популяций больших языковых моделей (LLM) через социальные взаимодействия. Эксперимент показал, что ленты с постами, ранжированными по лайкам, надёжно увеличивают лексическую конвергенцию — агенты начинают использовать похожие слова и выражения. Однако эффект не переносится на координацию мнений или захват позиций противоположной стороны: результаты были несогласованны между разными семействами моделей и темами. Основной вывод состоит в том, что простое изменение лексики ещё не гарантирует глубокие изменения в убеждениях или коллективное согласие среди LLM-агентов.

en.title: Peer Ranking Boosts Language Similarity, Not Opinion Alignment
en.desc: This paper investigates how peer-ranked feeds of synthetic large language model (LLM) agents affect their language use and coordination. The authors introduce a new testbed called PV-SST to analyze the behavior of LLM agents across various topics and model families. The results show that while peer-ranking increases lexical similarity among agents, it does not lead to consistent opinion alignment or coordination benefits. Overall, the study highlights that LLM agent behavior cannot be fully understood through traditional single-agent benchmarks, emphasizing the importance of peer interactions.

zh.title: 同伴排名提升词汇收敛，但未实现意见捕获
zh.desc: 本研究探讨了合成大型语言模型（LLM）代理的行为，发现同伴排名的社交平台对词汇收敛有显著影响，但并未可靠地实现意见捕获或协调优势。我们引入了PV-SST测试平台，通过448次实验，比较了不同主题和模型的表现。结果显示，经过同伴生成的点赞排名的帖子能提高最终回合的词汇相似度，但对意见变化的影响不明显。总体而言，研究表明在同伴排名的环境下，词汇收敛是一个可靠的结果，而不是普遍的意见捕获或协调优势。

papers.title: FlavourBench: Ranking Frontier Language Models with Executable Culinary Ground Truth
papers.abstract: Abstract FlavourBench evaluates language models on culinary portfolio tasks using executable ground truth, statistical rigor, and fully reproducible verification.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Open-ended language-model benchmarks usually inherit a judge: a human preference panel, another model, or a brittle exact-match key. We introduce FlavourBench, an automated benchmark in which a versioned culinary system supplies dense, executable ground truth. Each task presents eight ingredients and asks for a three-ingredient portfolio; before model execution, Epicure scores all 56 possible portfolios. We evaluate 27 frontier endpoints on an identical 534-task core spanning substitution, pairing, and constrained composition. Every ranked model has exactly 89 valid responses per panel and family (14,418 model-task cells total), eliminating differential missingness from the leaderboard. The FlavourBench Score is the equal-family mean of the frozen task scores. We use 50,000 anchor-cluster bootstrap replicates for simultaneous 95% score bands and 100,000 sign-flip draws for all 351 paired model contrasts, with Holm control. The two independently compiled panels correlate at r = 0.89 (rank rho = 0.80). Grok 4.6 has the largest point estimate at 65.1 (simultaneous 95% CI 61.0-69.2); 101 of 351 model pairs are resolved. The release includes the prompts, all portfolio score maps, raw responses, exact routes, content hashes, and an offline verifier that reconstructs every result.

ru.title: Объективная оценка языковых моделей через исполняемую кулинарную истину
ru.desc: FlavourBench представляет собой автоматизированный бенчмарк для оценки языковых моделей на кулинарных задачах с использованием исполняемой объективной истины вместо субъективных судей. Каждая задача предлагает выбрать три ингредиента из восьми и оценивает все 56 возможных комбинаций с помощью системы Epicure до выполнения моделью. Авторы протестировали 27 моделей на 534 задачах с использованием статистически строгого подхода: бутстреп-доверительные интервалы и множественное тестирование гипотез с поправкой Холма. Бенчмарк обеспечивает полную воспроизводимость благодаря публикации всех промптов, карт оценок портфелей, сырых ответов моделей и верификатора для реконструкции результатов.

en.title: Revolutionizing Culinary Model Evaluation with FlavourBench
en.desc: FlavourBench is a new automated benchmark designed to evaluate language models specifically on culinary tasks. It uses a unique system that provides executable ground truth, allowing for rigorous statistical analysis and reproducibility. The benchmark assesses models based on their ability to create three-ingredient portfolios from a set of eight ingredients, with scores calculated from all possible combinations. This method eliminates biases in evaluation by ensuring that every model is compared on an equal footing across a comprehensive set of tasks.

zh.title: FlavourBench：烹饪任务的自动化评估基准
zh.desc: FlavourBench 是一个评估语言模型在烹饪组合任务上的自动化基准。它使用可执行的真实数据和统计方法，确保结果的可重复性。每个任务提供八种成分，并要求生成三种成分的组合，同时对所有可能的组合进行评分。通过这种方式，FlavourBench 消除了评估中的偏差，提高了模型性能的比较准确性。

papers.title: Hadith computational science in the age of large language models: a critical narrative review
papers.abstract: Abstract Hadith computational science is evaluated as an evidence infrastructure challenge requiring integration of transformer and retrieval-based methods with expert validation and provenance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We examine how hadith computational science is being reshaped by transformer models, retrieval-grounded pipelines, and large language models (LLMs). Recent reviews document growth in the literature, but they do not yet provide a critical account of which advances are methodologically robust, which remain benchmark-bound, and which unresolved problems still limit scholarly use. We address this gap through a critical narrative review that combines critique of existing reviews, paper-level appraisal of representative original studies, and synthesis of Islamic scholar and domain-expert perspectives on authenticity, authority, and responsible use. We find uneven progress. Data resources have expanded, segmentation tasks have matured, narrator and source-verification problems are better formalized, and LLM-assisted workflows now support corpus-scale enrichment, multilingual access, and grounded evaluation. At the same time, progress remains constrained by narrow corpora, weak benchmark comparability, synthetic-to-real transfer gaps, narrator identity resolution, preprocessing fragility, limited reproducibility, and sparse expert-grounded validation. We show that important gaps lie beyond dominant benchmarks: non-canonical and obscure corpora, commentary and explanatory literature, cross-source links with Qur'an and seerah, and fiqh-facing evidence support. We argue that hadith computation should be assessed less as isolated model performance than as an evidence infrastructure problem requiring knowledge integration, provenance, and expert supervision. On this basis, we define a research agenda for making the field methodologically stronger and more useful to Islamic scholarship.

ru.title: От производительности моделей к инфраструктуре доказательств: переосмысление вычислительной науки о хадисах
ru.desc: В статье анализируется применение трансформер-моделей и больших языковых моделей (LLMs) в вычислительной науке о хадисах, выявляя как достигнутые успехи в расширении данных и автоматизации задач, так и остающиеся методологические проблемы. Авторы критически оценивают существующие подходы и показывают, что прогресс сдерживается узкими корпусами, слабой воспроизводимостью и недостатком экспертной валидации. Исследование предлагает рассматривать вычислительную обработку хадисов не как изолированную задачу оценки моделей, а как проблему инфраструктуры доказательств, требующей интеграции знаний и надзора экспертов. На основе этого подхода авторы формулируют научную повестку для укрепления методологии и повышения практической полезности для исламского богословия.

en.title: Transforming Hadith Science: Bridging Models and Expertise
en.desc: This paper discusses the challenges and advancements in hadith computational science, focusing on the integration of transformer models and retrieval-based methods. It highlights the need for expert validation and the importance of provenance in ensuring the authenticity of hadith data. The authors conduct a critical review of existing literature, identifying both progress and limitations in the field, such as issues with data resources and reproducibility. They propose a new research agenda aimed at strengthening methodological approaches and enhancing the utility of hadith computation for Islamic scholarship.

zh.title: 重塑圣训计算：知识整合与专家监督的必要性
zh.desc: 本论文探讨了圣训计算科学如何通过变换器模型和检索基础的方法进行重塑。我们发现，尽管数据资源和任务分割有所进展，但仍存在许多方法论上的不足和未解决的问题。特别是，现有的基准测试和数据集的局限性限制了学术界的有效使用。我们建议将圣训计算视为一个证据基础设施问题，需要知识整合、来源验证和专家监督，以推动该领域的发展。
